- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, apply downward bias correction — especially if recent prices are above 70, to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast decline by 5–10% to allow for mean reversion, not immediate reversal.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6) and forecast is erratic, smooth out 3–5 day moving average to reduce noise-driven overfitting.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to next forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, assume sentiment is misaligned — reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect “sentiment lag” effect.
